1.title: Talking about Languages
1.intro: Babak Saberian is a translator who works for IRIB. Today, he is hosting Meysam in his office. Meysam is a high school student. He is interviewing Mr. Saberian for his school project.

lines.speaker: Meysam
lines.text: Thank you Mr. Saberian for inviting me to your office.

lines.speaker: Mr. Saberian
lines.text: You're welcome!

lines.speaker: Meysam
lines.text: I heard you know three languages. Is that right?

lines.speaker: Mr. Saberian
lines.text: Well, actually four languages.

lines.speaker: Meysam
lines.text: Four! Really?! What languages do you know?

lines.speaker: Mr. Saberian
lines.text: Besides my mother tongue, Persian, I know English, French and Russian well.

lines.speaker: Meysam
lines.text: Interesting! And when did you learn them?

lines.speaker: Mr. Saberian
lines.text: I began learning English at school when I was thirteen. Then I began learning French in a language institute when I was fifteen. And I learned Russian when I was a university student in Moscow.

lines.speaker: Meysam
lines.text: Can you use all of them fluently?

lines.speaker: Mr. Saberian
lines.text: I know all of them well, but I use English more.

lines.speaker: Meysam
lines.text: OK. Do you think language learning should start as early as possible?

lines.speaker: Mr. Saberian
lines.text: My experience says interest and hard work are really more important than age.

lines.speaker: Meysam
lines.text: Hmm… that's an important point. May I know what your favorite language is? English, French, or Russian?

lines.speaker: Mr. Saberian
lines.text: To be honest, I enjoy using them all, but my favorite language is absolutely my mother tongue!

questions: Was Mr. Saberian living in a foreign country when he was 13?
How many languages do you know?

2.title: Talking about Lifestyle
2.intro: Sina and Behzad are old friends. They have not seen each other for about three months. Behzad has called Sina.

lines.speaker: Behzad
lines.text: Hi Sina. How is it going? I haven't seen you since Norooz.

lines.speaker: Sina
lines.text: Hi Behzad. Thanks for calling. I am home most of the time. I do different things like surfing the net and playing computer games.

lines.speaker: Behzad
lines.text: How about your free time? Going out, jogging, playing football,...?

lines.speaker: Sina
lines.text: Nope. I rarely go out and hang out with my friends.

lines.speaker: Behzad
lines.text: I see. Reza and I are going to Darband for climbing and walking this Thursday. We really like to see you. Will you come with us?

lines.speaker: Sina
lines.text: What?! Oh, no, I haven't been there for a long time. I prefer to stay home and watch my movies on the weekend. I've bought lots of things to eat, too.

lines.speaker: Behzad
lines.text: Come on! Stop being a couch potato! I guess you haven't exercised for a long time. I think you are a bit fat now.

lines.speaker: Sina
lines.text: Um… actually, you're right. I've gained five kilos in three months. I really do not like to move!

lines.speaker: Behzad
lines.text: See? I told you. Working with computers for a long time makes people sick and depressed. I've read about this somewhere.

lines.speaker: Sina
lines.text: All right. You won!… When and where should we meet?

questions: What does Sina do at home?

3.title: Shopping Handicrafts
3.intro: Listen to the conversation between Reza and a tourist.

lines.speaker: Reza
lines.text: How can I help you, sir?

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.text: I am looking for some Iranian handicrafts.

lines.speaker: Reza
lines.text: Here you can find a range of Iranian hand-made products, from carpets to pottery and tilework, but we don't sell metalwork.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.text: I'd like to buy a Persian carpet, but it seems too expensive.

lines.speaker: Reza
lines.text: The price depends on its size. Instead, you can take an Isfahan Termeh or a Qashqai Gabbeh.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.text: Wow! How touching this Gabbeh is! How much is it?

lines.speaker: Reza
lines.text: It is 85 dollars. If you buy more than 100 dollars, you'll get a 20 percent discount. You can take this calligraphic tile for only 30 dollars.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.text: Well, I'll take both. Please pack them for me.

lines.speaker: Reza
lines.text: Yes, sure.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.text: Do you work for this shop? Who has made these beautiful items?

lines.speaker: Reza
lines.text: Actually, it is my father's workshop and store. I work here after school. All my family members work here to help our family business.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.text: Well done! How lucky you are to work in such a lovely shop. I really appreciate the culture and art of Iran.

lines.speaker: Reza
lines.text: Thank you very much. If you are interested in knowing more about our products, you can check this booklet.

questions: What is the most famous handicraft of your city or village?
